title: Muscles & movement
examples: What is the difference between a joint and a muscle?
How does the bicep muscle help you to bend your elbow?
Can you explain the sliding filament theory in simple terms?

explain.say: Today we are learning about how your body moves so well.

items: Muscles provide the force for movement.

explain.say: Muscles often work in pairs called antagonistic pairs.
A joint is the place where two or more bones meet.
The sliding filament theory explains muscle contraction happening.
When you bend your arm, the bicep contracts and the tricep relaxes.
A real life example is kicking a football with your leg.

faq.q: Why do muscles need to work in pairs?
faq.a: Antagonistic pairs keep movement controlled and efficient. When one muscle pulls, the other must relax or pull in the opposite direction.
asks: What is the role of opposing muscles?

faq.a: No, joints have different structures for different movements. For example, the shoulder allows a wide range of motion.
asks: Does the knee move like the wrist?

faq.q: What are the filaments in muscle contraction?
faq.a: The filaments are thin strands of protein called actin and thick strands called myosin. The interaction between them causes the muscle to shorten.
asks: What proteins cause muscle to pull?
How does the sliding filament theory work?

faq.a: Yes, muscle contraction requires energy, which comes from the breakdown of stored energy molecules in the cells.

faq.q: If I only use one muscle, what happens?
faq.a: Movement would be jerky or unstable because the opposing muscles are needed for smooth control. The pairs balance the action.
asks: Can I move smoothly without opposites?
Why do I need both muscles to work?

facts: Muscles attach to bones via tough bands of connective tissue called tendons.
The bicep and tricep are common examples of antagonistic pairs.
Joints allow movement by separating bones at specific points.
Muscle contraction occurs when myosin filaments pull on actin filaments.

quiz.say: When you straighten your arm, which pair of muscles is primarily working?
quiz.why: The triceps is the extensor, so it must contract to straighten the arm.

wrong.0: This describes bending the arm, not straightening it.
wrong.1: Muscles are antagonistic, so they rarely contract equally in one direction.
wrong.2: Movement requires the active pulling force from at least one muscle.

quiz.say: Which structure allows the bones of the wrist to move flexibly?
quiz.why: Synovial joints are designed for a wide range of movement, like the wrist.

wrong.1: Pivot joints only allow rotation, like turning your head.
wrong.2: Hinge joints only allow movement in one plane, like a door.
wrong.3: This is a type of joint, but synovial is the general category for this flexibility.

quiz.say: In the sliding filament theory, what pulls the actin filaments?
quiz.why: The thick myosin filaments have heads that bind to and pull the thin actin filaments.

wrong.1: The myosin heads are described as doing the pulling action in this model.
wrong.2: Calcium ions are signals that trigger the interaction, they are not the pulling force.
wrong.3: The nerve impulse is the signal; the proteins do the physical pulling.
